entries.title: Zooming a PDF no longer throws the reader back to page 1, and the reading position survives a relaunch
entries.notes: Go to page 2 of a PDF, zoom in, and the reader jumped back to page 1; quit and reopen and you were on page 1 rather than where you left off. Traced in the real app, the chain was: a zoom transiently collapses the scroll container so the browser clamps scrollTop to 0; the scroll observer (updateCurPage) reads that half-resized layout and publishes page 1 as reader view state; that write mutates the pdf route, which rebuilds resolvedTarget, which re-fires the navigation effect, which navigates to page 1 — locking it in. A load-time fit-width scale change made it worse by capturing a zoom anchor on page 1 that settleZoom re-asserted AFTER the reader had deliberately moved to page 2. Four coupled changes in src/components/PdfViewer.tsx: suppress the scroll-derived page while a zoom is settling; anchor a zoom to the page being read rather than a whole-document scroll ratio; let an explicit navigation supersede a pending zoom anchor; and stop navigateToTarget silently substituting page 1 when the target page's wrapper is merely not mounted yet. Evidence: fail-before 2/3 on the exact symptom against master's binary affe9be1, pass-after 8/8 on the branch binary. This is also the defect behind the e2e-pdf-routes flake that had it quarantined.

entries.title: Opening a link to the PDF you are already reading keeps your place instead of jumping to page 1
entries.notes: Clicking an asset link to the PDF already open in that pane — a plain ![](....pdf) with no page and no highlight — threw away the reader's position and the highlight overlay. openPdf's existing-tab branch published a PDF navigation intent unconditionally, and an intent IS a request to move: the viewer's navigation effect resolves target.page ?? 1 and clears the highlight overlay, so an empty intent navigated to page 1. Publishing it only when a page or a highlight is actually requested is the fix (src/panes.ts). Necessity gate proven at the unit layer: 'reopening the PDF you are already reading keeps your place' fails pre-fix with the intent rebuilt as {page: undefined}, and its companion test proves a real page or highlight request still navigates. e2e-pdf-logseq already encoded this exact OG-parity contract ('reopening the already-current resource without a page/highlight intent is a no-op, not an implicit jump to page 1') and master fails it: with the one-line change reverted in the same tree, the journey dies at that assertion with {overlay: null, target: null}. An earlier batch mistook this fix for a regression in a later Close PDF step; the real cause was that the close helper assumed one click empties the pane, which is false when the journey deliberately keeps two PDF tabs open.

entries.title: Accepting a page/block-ref completion while editing inside an existing ref rewrites the whole ref, leaving no stray closing bracket (Logseq parity)
entries.notes: GH #199. Editing inside an already-closed [[word]] (e.g. autopaired [[second]], arrow-left, type 'first ' -> [[first |second]]) and accepting a completion left a stray ]] ([[first]]second]]) because Block.tsx replaceTrigger only swallowed the closing pair when it sat IMMEDIATELY at the caret (ref.value.slice(t.end,t.end+2)===pair). OG-verified (og@6e7afa8, findings in tine-agents specs notes): OG's query range is [[->caret (matches Tine's detectTrigger, unchanged), but on accept OG scans forward from the caret to the ref's closer (:end-pattern ]]), strips it (postfix-fn) and rewrites the whole region. Fix: new pure refCompletionEnd(value,end,insertedText) in autocomplete.ts scans forward on the CURRENT LINE for the closer matching the completion's suffix (]]/))/}}), returning just past it or the caret when none ahead; replaceTrigger now uses it. Covers page AND block refs (same latent defect) and the latent end-caret ]]]] doubling. Not a regression: latent since the autocomplete feature shipped (e54ad36e, 2026-06-14). Fail-before proven (pre-fix immediate-only range yields [[first]]second]]); 7 unit cases (mid/end/unclosed/block/line-bounded/non-ref/reporter-integration); Block.referenceAuthoring + tagAutocomplete + selectionWrap render tests still green (wiring regression guard). Added store.mergeWithNext as an exact structural mirror of mergeWithPrev (visible-only concat, survivor keeps identity/hidden props, absorbed block's id:: adopted only when survivor lacks one, children reparented, single merge undo unit, cross-page refusal). Arrows require collapsed caret and no modifiers (Ctrl/Meta word jumps and Shift selection stay native); Delete refuses to merge into or out of annotation/calc blocks and is a no-op at the last block. Left/Right stay within the loaded outline (no journal feed extension, unlike ArrowDown).

entries.title: Journal-title carry buttons swap today's pull-in actions for push-to-today when the calendar rolls over
entries.notes: Martin internal report: after midnight, yesterday's journal kept showing today's carry buttons (Carry from previous day / Carry last N days) instead of switching to 'Carry unfinished tasks → today'. Root cause: CarryActions.isToday compared the page name against journalTitle(new Date()) evaluated once at mount — nothing reactive, so the choice never re-evaluated. Fix: journal.ts gains a reactive currentDayKey (one-shot DST-safe timeout chain re-armed each midnight, plus focus/visibility resync for sleeping machines) and localDateFromDayKey so the compared title derives from the SAME reactive value; CarryActions reads it. Fail-before proven in-tree: with the pre-fix bare new Date() comparison, only the two rollover tests fail while the three static-shape tests pass.

entries.title: Delete/Backspace over a rendered (not-editing) block text selection deletes that text, matching OG contenteditable
entries.notes: Martin internal report: selecting block text and pressing Delete/Backspace sometimes does nothing, seemingly speed-dependent. Real-app matrix (27 cases, WebKitGTK) showed editor selections always delete; the dead keypress is a RENDERED-view (not-editing) text selection — Tine separates rendered view from textarea, the drag is treated as text selection not a click-to-edit, and Delete reaches no editor (selection stays, nothing changes). Fix: window-capture Delete/Backspace with a non-collapsed selection inside one block's rendered wrapper maps endpoints to source offsets (render/spans.ts) and splices visible text via the normal setRaw path (undo, dirty), then opens the editor at the join point. Conservative no-ops: cross-block selections, selections inside atomic constructs (links/chips — coarse spans snap to the same edge), annotation/calc blocks, read-only pages, blocks already being edited, modals open, unmapped endpoints. Side observation (untouched): WebKit smart-delete on native double-click word selections eats one trailing space uniformly (fast and slow).

entries.title: Right-sidebar open items and left-sidebar favorites reorder via pointer drag within their own list while clicking, middle-click, context menu, close and scrolling behavior are preserved, and order persists through the existing owners
entries.notes: GH #211. New shared helper src/components/rowReorder.ts implements the repo's hand-rolled pointer-drag pattern (HTML5 DnD unreliable in WebKitGTK): 4px threshold, data-row-index rows, half-row before/after insertion, and armed click suppression for the drop's synthesized click. Right-sidebar rows use moveRightSidebarItem (persists via setRightSidebar to localStorage+session); favorites use moveFavorite (persists via persistFavorites to config.edn). Reorder is within-list only; no cross-list drag. Component tests assert order, persistence, sub-threshold click preservation, and swallowing of the drop's click. Keyboard reorder (Alt+arrows) is a deliberate follow-up, out of this batch's proportionality budget. Fail-before proven by manager mutation probe at integration (2026-08-06): disabling moveFavorite fails 2/3 of Sidebar.favReorder.test.tsx while the sub-threshold-click test correctly still passes. Tests were written after the implementation in the delegated lane; the probe supplies the causal evidence.

entries.title: A graph can have a configured home page that opens in the primary tab on ordinary graph opens, skipping silently when it no longer resolves
entries.notes: GH #245 and #269. homePage.ts now uses graph metadata backed by Logseq's :default-home {:page ...} entry in logseq/config.edn, with a guarded one-time migration from the former per-device app-settings string. graph.ts's loadGraphPath opens it via openPage(name, page, {inPlace:true}) only on first-bind / graph-switch loads — never on same-graph force refresh; a missing page falls back silently. Settings Graph tab rows expose pick-from-existing-pages (quickSwitch, pages only), a stale-value hint, and Clear. Fail-before for the navigation behavior was proven by manager mutation probe at integration (2026-08-06); fail-before for graph ownership was proven by src/homePage.test.ts returning the stale device-local value instead of graph metadata on the pre-fix source.

entries.title: Built-in themes recolor the dark-mode viewport and page as well as secondary sidebar surfaces, while custom.css remains the final override
entries.notes: GH #401. The dependency-free startup frame used a high-specificity html[data-theme=dark] body rule with fixed default colors. Theme variables changed correctly, but the body retained Tine's default dark background and text while secondary surfaces recolored. The startup rule now uses --bg-primary and --text-primary with the same fixed colors only as pre-CSS fallbacks. The browser gate measures every built-in theme in light and dark modes and proves custom.css still wins after the managed theme layer.

entries.title: A System appearance choice follows the OS/WebView prefers-color-scheme signal immediately and live, while manual Light/Dark ignore it
entries.notes: GH #193. appearancePreference (light/dark/system) persists via the existing localStorage theme key; the resolved theme() signal stays light/dark so capture-window broadcast, gallery themes and Android bars are unchanged. The matchMedia change listener attaches only while System is selected and detaches on manual selection. Fallback without the signal is light, Tine's default. Existing saved light/dark values are untouched.

entries.title: The /That day slash command inserts a page reference to the containing journal page's semantic date in the configured journal title format
entries.notes: GH #252. A new 'That day' slash command (action 'thatday') resolves the containing page's kind and name via pageByName. On a journal page, parseJournalTitle extracts the semantic date (trying the configured format, the default, and yyyy-MM-dd), then journalTitle formats it in the current configured format and inserts [[formatted]]. On a non-journal page the trigger is cleared and a toast explains the constraint. The inserted text is ordinary durable block content.

entries.title: The bundled app scripts parse and run on pre-16.4 Safari/WKWebView (macOS 12) instead of dying at startup with an invalid-regex SyntaxError and a white screen
entries.notes: GH #256. Debug log showed Safari's parse-time 'invalid group specifier name' error: src/mock.ts shipped the bundle's only regex lookbehind in the modulepreloaded app chunk. Guard test greps all src sources for lookbehind (failed on mock.ts:65 pre-fix); tagsOf now uses a prefix-capture group with identical behavior (old-vs-new output compared on 10 samples). Real macOS 12 WKWebView confirmation not possible in this environment. REVIEW CORRECTION (manager, integration): the first fix replaced the negative lookbehind with a leading capture group `(^|[^\[])#...`, which READS as equivalent but CONSUMES the preceding character, so with a global regex a tag written immediately after another one had nothing left to match its prefix against and was silently dropped -- `#a#b` yielded only `a`, and `#[[x]]#y` only `x`, in 4 of 13 probed inputs. The lookbehind is zero-width; the replacement must be too. Corrected to check the preceding character AFTER the match, which keeps the test zero-width, and src/mockTags.test.ts now calls the real tagsOf (not a copy of its regex) and fails against the first fix.

entries.title: In-page find (Ctrl+F) reveal centers the exact occurrence, not merely its block, when the block is taller than the viewport
entries.notes: GH #253. Matches were already tracked per-occurrence and highlighted; only the reveal scrolled the whole block to center. revealInPageFindMatch now resolves the active occurrence's Range rect (same ordinal as the highlight layer) and adjusts the nearest vertical scroller to center it, falling back to the coarse block scroll when no DOM-text range exists (edit-mode textarea). WebKitGTK scroll behavior not runtime-verified here; jsdom test with stubbed range rects proves the semantic scroll delta (fail-before: scrollTop stayed 0 pre-fix). REVIEW CORRECTION (manager, integration): nearestVerticalScroller accepted any ancestor with overflow-y auto/scroll, including one that does not actually overflow. Adjusting such an element's scrollTop is a no-op, and the function still reported success, so the caller skipped its block-level scrollIntoView fallback and the occurrence stayed off-screen -- strictly worse than the behaviour this change replaced. It now requires scrollHeight > clientHeight; the existing jsdom fixture had to start modelling a scroller that really can scroll. KNOWN COVERAGE GAP: a regression test for the non-scrolling-ancestor branch was attempted and withdrawn -- revealInPageFindMatch did not reach the scroll step under that jsdom fixture and chasing it was harness work, not product work (AGENTS.md economy rule). The guard is reasoned from the DOM contract and is not covered by a test.

entries.title: The native Windows updater reaches the signed manifest and installer assets through the affected network route
entries.notes: GH #241. Negative v0.6.94 and v0.6.97 reporter follow-ups revoke the native-transport fix claim: WebView2 reaches GitHub, while the Rust updater fails fetching latest.json before manifest parsing, target selection, signature verification, download, or installation. Native TLS and Reqwest's manual Windows system-proxy feature are present but are structural evidence only; PAC/WPAD or integrated-auth proxy behavior remains a hypothesis pending a representative Windows reproduction or sanitized causal chain. Do not mark this covered from compilation or feature-tree checks.

entries.title: Updater failures expose a privacy-safe stage and cause while retaining a sanitized opt-in causal chain
entries.notes: GH #241. The old toast claimed the debug log contained the error, but ordinary diagnostics recorded no updater event and the console exposed only an undifferentiated outer error. Manifest fetch/parse/target selection, download/signature/install, and relaunch now map to fixed stage/cause tokens in the privacy-safe report. The bounded opt-in chain removes URLs, queries, credentials, and local paths; the failure toast links to Diagnostics and names --debug as the detailed path. Fail-before: no diagnostic event or sanitized chain was emitted.

entries.title: Startup and manual update checks share one offer and installation still requires explicit confirmation
entries.notes: GH #241. The v0.6.97 negative follow-up concerns native transport, not the independent prompt behavior. Startup and explicit checks replace the existing offer rather than stacking dialogs, checking never installs, and only the Install update action invokes the signed native updater.

entries.title: A Windows x86 build without signed updater metadata offers the exact manual package path instead of an impossible install
entries.notes: GH #241. The reporter's v0.6.97 diagnostics identify an x86 process, while release-layout intentionally omits windows-i686 updater entries during the experimental GH #275 pilot. The architecture is now read from the native process before presenting an action; x86 receives a sticky manual-download explanation and never calls updater.check. Fail-before: every desktop architecture received Install update even when the signed manifest could not contain its target.

entries.title: Enter and multiline paste inside a $$ … $$ environment keep the block together instead of splitting it
entries.notes: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM OG, approved by Martin 2026-08-09. OG's Enter dwim (frontend/util/thingatpt.cljs admonition&src-at-point) recognises only ``` and #+BEGIN_, so OG also splits the bullet and breaks the environment; the reporter is asking for an improvement, not restored parity. The v0.6.92 Enter fix was too narrow: the reporter's post-release follow-up proved that pasting LaTeX containing a blank line into the same environment still segmented it into outline blocks. The shared syntax-sensitive editor decision now uses caretInDisplayMath for paste as well as Enter, including selection replacement; ordinary blank-line prose still segments normally. The parser, on-disk bytes and property classification remain untouched. Necessity gate proven: the exact reporter paste tests fail before the paste predicate is widened.

entries.title: Clicking a task marker label uses Logseq's open-state toggle and never removes DONE
entries.notes: OG source at 6e7afa8eb separates marker-switch (components/block.cljs:1861) from keyboard cycle-marker-state (util/marker.cljs:40): label clicks toggle TODO/DOING and LATER/NOW, while DONE is not clickable; keyboard cycling may still reach DONE and then remove the marker. Tine had wired both block and Sheet label clicks to its keyboard cycle, so clicking DONE silently removed completion. The click helper is now separate, preserves the existing logbook transition machinery, and is shared by ordinary blocks and Sheet state cells. Keyboard and checkbox behavior are unchanged. The reporter confirmed this exact OG behavior and accepted it.

entries.title: Generic custom.css image sizing does not constrain the full-screen lightbox
entries.notes: Graph custom.css intentionally loads after Tine's stylesheet, so a generic `img { width: 320px; height: auto }` thumbnail rule also constrained `.lightbox-img`. The lightbox now owns its geometry through the more-specific `.lightbox-overlay > img.lightbox-img` rule with auto width/height, viewport maxima and object-fit contain. A later generic img rule remains effective for inline thumbnails but loses only on the dedicated lightbox surface; users can still target `.lightbox-img` explicitly if desired.

entries.title: Native page selections exclude Add block and reference-section UI labels
entries.notes: The reporter's concrete copied suffixes are UI labels, not page content: `+ Add block`, `Linked References`, and `Unlinked References`. The trailing target and every references header now opt out of native selection in both standard and WebKit-prefixed CSS, so mouse/touch selection can cross the page without copying application chrome. This deliberately does not attempt nonstandard region-containment semantics; actual reference block content remains selectable.

entries.title: Native page selections exclude page action control labels (carry-over buttons, tag-table toggle, guide copy, ⋯ trigger)
entries.notes: Internal report (Martin, 2026-08-25): texts of page action controls such as the journal carry-over buttons became part of ordinary dragged text selections. The title-row controls — carry-over buttons, tag-table toggle, guide copy button and the ⋯ page-actions trigger — now opt out of native selection in both standard and WebKit-prefixed CSS while remaining ordinary activatable buttons (pointer events and keyboard focus are untouched; the icon-only favorite star contributes no selection text and is intentionally out of scope). Page and block content remains selectable.

entries.title: Copy / export as… offers an explicit preserve-Markdown/Org content choice next to cleaned plain text
entries.notes: Current-state preflight: the reporter's v0.6.93 already contained the Content choice (Rendered cleaned / Source preserved, shipped 2026-07-02), but nothing on the modal said 'Markdown' or 'plain text', so the preserve option was undiscoverable — the harm is the invisible choice, while the transformation already preserved the source syntax. The Content buttons now name the outcome: Plain text (cleaned, default retained) and Markdown — format-aware, so an Org forest offers Org — with hints echoing the issue's preserve/clean wording; the two moot-toggle tooltips use the same vocabulary. Modal render tests prove both directions at the block entry point (explicit labels present; preserve keeps **bold**, [[links]], property lines, ==highlight==; default cleans them), the page entry point shares the one modal (ContextMenu.test.tsx covers both routings), and pure exportText tests pin verbatim source syntax inside the requested exported outline for representative inline formatting, nested blocks, and Org emphasis/drawers.

entries.title: Navigating to a block nested inside collapsed parents expands its ancestors, scrolls to it and highlights it
entries.notes: openPageAtBlock polled the DOM for .ls-block[data-block-id] up to 20x50ms, but Block.tsx renders no children for a collapsed parent, so a Ctrl+Shift+K block result inside a collapsed subtree could never match and the poll timed out silently. store.expandAncestors expands the target's own ancestor chain (not unrelated collapsed blocks) as ONE undo step, persisting collapsed:: exactly as a manual expand does. Necessity gate proven: two of the three tests fail on the pre-fix tree. Reporter supplied an AI-written root cause; it was independently confirmed against router.ts:596 and Block.tsx:577 before implementing.

entries.title: Linked and Unlinked References keep the user's expand/collapse choice when the page subtree re-renders
entries.notes: Reported on a >5,000-page graph: a page with ~173 linked references collapsed its own section while scrolling or expanding a group, while ~48 references behaved. The flag was a component-local signal, so ANY remount of the page subtree reset it, and OG_REFERENCE_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD=100 makes 'reset' mean collapsed — which is precisely the 48-fine/173-broken split. Moving the state to src/referenceSectionState.ts makes the symptom impossible whatever causes the remount, which is what the reporter asked for ('stay in current existing state no matter what'). Memory-only: OG's collapse-above-100 default still applies on a fresh start, and resetStore clears it on graph switch. NOT YET REPRODUCED on a real large graph — the remount trigger (suspected Page.tsx pagesToRender() going transiently empty) is unconfirmed; keep reported until a large-graph user or the Direct Files perf audit confirms.

entries.title: Ctrl+O opens the page at the caret, Ctrl+Shift+O opens it in the sidebar
entries.notes: OG parity gap: OG binds :editor/follow-link to mod+o and :editor/open-link-in-sidebar to mod+shift+o (frontend/modules/shortcut/config.cljs:214/:217); Tine had no mod+o at all. The 'which link' rule is transcribed from OG's thingatpt.cljs extract-nearest-link-from-text, including its surprising part: OG collects EVERY candidate in the block and picks the one nearest the caret, so a caret anywhere in a block with one link still follows it. URLs are included for follow and deliberately excluded for the sidebar, matching OG's two call sites. Block refs are best-effort: a bare ((uuid)) in raw text carries no page, so a block outside the loaded working set is not found - the same give-up OG's open-link-in-sidebar! does when db/get-page misses. FAIL-BEFORE is an absence (no mod+o binding existed), verified by grep.

entries.title: Android Back never exits after an unverified managed shutdown and remains owned before JavaScript is ready
entries.notes: An Android AppPlugin listener could fall back to WebView history or activity finish before JavaScript subscribed, while the process-wide managed shutdown helper collapsed terminal and safe outcomes and could exit after a terminal runtime. The repair introduces a native SafeBack owner that consumes all Back events unless its own listener is ready, and a typed process preparation result: only Safe may exit; Refused reopens the editor only when no managed slot was verified; Partial or an unknown transport result remains shielded and retries native preparation alone. JS tests cover listener lifecycle and the zero-progress/partial/unknown retry matrix; Rust tests cover sorted stop-at-first-refusal aggregation, terminal rejection and Safe retry. Physical Android compilation and hardware Back remain hosted-CI/device gates.

entries.title: Managed-storage runtime status, progress and failure reasons update the app and open Storage & sync panel for the current graph only
entries.notes: Confirmed UI audit H1 at dc82d0c4: watcher.rs emitted sparse-v2-status, sparse-v2-tick and sparse-v2-error, but the frontend subscribed only to sparse-v2-changed. The Settings panel therefore retained its open-time status snapshot and the runtime's explicit failure reason was invisible. A single app-owned typed bridge now updates both surfaces, preserves the native reason text, and accepts an event only when its binding generation matches the currently bound graph. Direct-file managed-sync-error and graph-watch-error listeners remain unchanged.

entries.title: A graph open that stalls or fails reports its phase and offers retry, another graph, copied details, and an escape back to Direct Files
entries.notes: Before this cycle neither src/startupRecovery.ts nor src/components/StartupRecovery.tsx existed (both are added against v0.6.92), so a stalled open painted nothing and offered no action; that is the literal pre-state rather than a reconstructed one. The overlay appears only after STARTUP_PROGRESS_VISIBLE_MS so an ordinary fast open still shows nothing, becomes role=alertdialog on recovery, and states that no managed-storage data has been discarded. The Return-to-Direct-Files action is gated on a real native lookup authority token (nativeAttempt > 0), so it is never offered for a graph that was never enrolled. Copy details uses the resilient clipboard transport because recovery must not depend exclusively on the native invoke bridge it is diagnosing. Declining recovery resumes the open rather than stranding the app. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Indent, outdent and repeated moves on a multi-block selection apply as one shared-store command and one undo unit
entries.notes: F1 indent/outdent previously removed and reinserted each selected root separately; roots drawn from different original sibling arrays are now removed once and inserted in visible order. F2 collapses a run of Up/Down moves into one command family that closes on idle, a three-second maximum, a changed selected-root set, an Undo or Redo, an unrelated edit, or a page reload, so one Undo reverses the move rather than one block of it. Read-only refusals are preserved exactly: a feed-spanning selection containing a read-only day is refused and dirties neither page, and a writable feed-spanning outdent leaves the other day byte-identical and clean. Zoom-scope containment is asserted on both operations. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Pasting many blocks with preserved IDs makes one loaded-document identity pass instead of one per candidate
entries.notes: The superseded per-id predicate rescanned every loaded key and every loaded raw for each incoming identity, so cost grew with candidates times page size. The batched helper is asserted through an explicit work receipt (src/clipboardWorkProbe.ts): 200+ preserved-ID paste and redo candidates each record exactly one loaded_identity_pass, and incoming_identity_ids_checked stays fixed as the loaded document grows. Fail-closed behaviour is unchanged and independently asserted: an internally duplicated moved payload is rejected before the loaded document is consulted, and both the Markdown id:: and Org :id: raw forms are still matched without requiring an Org drawer. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Property autocomplete remains usable when authored entirely from the keyboard
entries.notes: OG moves the caret before a line-opening :: delimiter and searches the property name to its left. Tine previously left the caret after ::, so the first name character produced malformed ::a text, closed the popup, and could surface repeated backend error notifications. Coverage exercises the real input-event lifecycle: :: moves the caret left; typed characters filter without closing; Create is discoverable at the top; selection enters value search; a directly authored key:: followed by space also enters value search; and comma starts a new value search with already-authored values excluded. Facet lookup failure is contained to the optional autocomplete surface and cannot reject the editor input event.

entries.title: Dragging a block into the deep target zone makes it a child of that block
entries.notes: Tine's pointer drag implementation exposed only before/after sibling targets, so Windows was not exceptional: no platform could express OG's nested drop. OG 6e7afa8eb chooses :nested when the pointer is more than 50px inside the target block and moves the dragged roots under that target. The shared pointer path now uses that same intent threshold and a distinct child indicator. The target-relative store transaction accepts child placement for one or many normalized selected roots, appends them after existing children, preserves subtrees, page reassignment and order-list inheritance, rejects self/descendant cycles through the existing plan, and remains one undo/redo unit. Cross-page managed moves transmit the equivalent child placement to the storage actor.

entries.title: Custom CSS can enable Inter OpenType stylistic sets and character variants
entries.notes: The custom CSS property itself reached the computed style correctly; the bundled @fontsource/inter per-script static subsets lacked ss02 and every other Inter stylistic set. Tine now ships the audited full upstream Inter 4.1 variable faces under the same public Inter family name, preserving existing themes and user CSS while restoring ss01-ss08 and cv01-cv14. The regression pins both upstream font hashes and verifies the public family and variable-weight declarations; the production build separately proves Vite emits both faces.

entries.title: The release E2E distinguishes undelivered native ArrowDown input from broken page-header traversal
entries.notes: Release run 31569006329 observed no keydown witness despite the expected header activeElement; the unchanged candidate passed the rerun and six focused repetitions. The journey now uses a real pointer action to transfer native focus, proves document focus/editor/caret readiness, and retries locally only when no key witness arrives. The suite runner may retry that isolated scenario once on the explicit E2E_NATIVE_INPUT_UNDELIVERED receipt. An unmodified ArrowDown witnessed on the expected header but failing to enter the first body block remains an immediate blocking product failure.

entries.title: The release E2E distinguishes an unready GTK upload chooser from an upload product failure
entries.notes: The unchanged v0.6.93 candidate passed the same literal upload journey twice and failed once after a blind chooser activation/type/120ms sequence. The harness already launches Openbox, so a missing window manager was not the current cause. It now proves the chooser is visible and EWMH-active, submits the absolute path, observes closure, and only reactivates/sends Open while the chooser remains visibly mapped. The suite runner may retry the isolated scenario once only on E2E_NATIVE_CHOOSER_INPUT_UNDELIVERED. If the chooser closes but the graph asset or Markdown write is absent, the existing blocking product assertion remains unchanged.

entries.title: The release E2E waits for semantic block-embed content before interacting with it
entries.notes: The v0.6.92 journey clicked as soon as embed macro roots existed, while cross-page descendants populated asynchronously; adding an unrelated await moved the failure between disclosure and arrow/delete. The semantic readiness repair then exposed a deterministic product defect: multiple visible refs/embeds to the same initially unloaded page raced activation; one loaded the exact page, while siblings treated their expected stale-install refusal as permanent failure and stayed shallow. LiveRefGroup now rechecks the exact loaded kind/path after every installation attempt, so a sibling winner hydrates all groups while a different page/path remains refused. A render regression forces two concurrent activation promises and proves both descendants render with one retained activation. The release journey waits for exactly the identities/content/disclosure controls it will operate on, asserts no timing or pixels, and is restored to stable blocking coverage.

entries.title: Setting up or joining managed sync reopens the actor retired by the enrollment cut before reporting success
entries.notes: The real two-device journey reached healthy local activation, then the first explicit share cut stopped its actor by design and the Tauri command immediately queried that retired handle, returning sync actor is unavailable. Share and already-managed join now reopen the durable post-enrollment runtime, prove its ordinary page inventory/load boundary, and publish a new exact-generation graph slot before returning success. That repair exposed a second product defect: a bounded watcher scan could acknowledge one epoch while newer observations remained pending, but an AdmittedNoop/Complete tick scheduled no continuation and a quiet graph supplied no new inotify edge. The watcher now consults the actor's post-tick pending bit, drains all retained epochs without a timer guess, and still leaves a truly quiet actor asleep. The source regressions pin cut -> reopen -> exact publish ordering and pending-epoch continuation; the real two-device journey remains the release-blocking semantic proof.

entries.title: A peer edit delivered into managed storage becomes visible without waiting for an unrelated filesystem event
entries.notes: The two-device journey delivered device B's edit into device A's graph-local provider tree while device A was stopped. On reopen, device A discovered the delivery (provider_pending=3) while its watcher was idle (pending=false, latest_enqueue=2, acknowledged=2), and the peer edit never appeared. The Tauri sparse scheduler decided continuation from the tick result plus the actor's watcher pending bit only, so a tick that settled a watcher epoch read as a quiet graph and cleared the retry schedule; a quiet graph produces no further inotify edge for bytes another device wrote, so the delivered work was stranded forever. The actor now publishes provider_runnable alongside provider_pending - the exact predicate tick consults, not the broad inventory that legitimately never reaches zero while durable publication intents remain - and the scheduler continues while SyncRuntimeStatusSnapshot::has_runnable_work() is true. A tick that reports Idle while still naming runnable provider work is paced by the ordinary backoff schedule instead of the progress cadence, so a blocked causal dependency cannot become a poll loop, and a genuinely quiet actor still arms no timer at all. Source regressions pin arrival across the delivery/reopen cut, arrival to a running receiver, a multi-item drain to zero with interleaved page reads, and the idle direction; the real two-device journey remains the release-blocking semantic proof.

entries.title: A peer edit that lands in managed SQLite always reaches the Markdown file, even when a local external edit is admitted in the same window
entries.notes: On a running receiving device, an inbound provider batch could be applied to SQLite while its Markdown file was never written. The receiver-local projection decided whether a delivered foreign intent was still the live authority by comparing the intent's post-frontier with the page's WHOLE current merged frontier. An ordinary local external admission landing in the same window commits its own batch, which advances the shared page-catalog document, so the delivered intent stopped matching a page it never touched; the intent was then treated as superseded historical evidence and dropped. Nothing else owned that path, so the page existed in ListPages at the right path with no file on disk, clean_shutdown still returned Safe, and a reopen with a full re-drive never repaired it - durable data-visibility loss, since Markdown is the interchange truth for Direct Files parity and for every external tool. A receiver that cannot prove the delivered intent is still current now projects the page's CURRENT accepted state instead of skipping it (idempotent: a genuinely superseded page renders to the bytes already on disk), projects at the path the accepted state names rather than the intent's stale one, and retains the obligation as a published continuation when neither the intent nor the current state can be authorized. Source regressions pin creates, edits and cross-page moves under that interleaving, each with a Safe shutdown and a clean reopen. NOT covered here: provider-delivered DELETES and RENAMES never converge on the clean runtime at all - with or without the interleaving - because the receiver-local tombstone authorization still requires the retired pre-0.7 durable endpoint history store; that is a separate open defect.

entries.title: The Android Back gesture reaches Tine's rungs and closes the Settings modal instead of silently stepping WebView history
entries.notes: Reported internally by Martin: with the Settings modal open, the hardware Back gesture did not close it. The frontend rungs were never at fault - dispatchAndroidBack, the transient registry and Settings' three-rung dismiss all behave correctly in the real app composition, which is why the defect survived. androidx's OnBackPressedDispatcher hands a gesture to the LAST-ADDED enabled callback, and Tauri's core AppPlugin adds its own from its Kotlin constructor, which runs on the Rust startup thread tao spawns inside Rust.create() - after MainActivity.onCreate has already returned. AppPlugin therefore sat ABOVE Tine's SafeBack owner, took its no-listener branch (Tine registers android-safe-back on its own plugin, never back-button on Tauri's) and answered Back with WebView.goBack() whenever the WebView had history. The mobile router pushes one history entry per navigation, so after the user's first navigation every Back popped a route BEHIND whatever was on screen and no rung ever ran; before that first navigation canGoBack() is false, AppPlugin re-dispatches and Back works, which is why this read as intermittent. SafeBackPlugin now claims ownership from its own constructor and again from load(), both strictly later than every plugin registered so far. The frontend semantic regression is blocking and green. The native WebView instrumentation remains in the Android runtime job but is explicitly quarantined after the 2026-08-22 two-attempt stop-loss: on GitHub's software-graphics emulator the process aborts before any JUnit assertion with Android libc reporting pthread_mutex_lock on a destroyed mutex. Managed-storage activation/crash-recovery tests run in a separate instrumentation lifetime and remain fully blocking.

entries.title: Favorites can be arranged into a tree of named groups nested to any depth, surviving restart, sync and page renames, without changing which pages are favorited
entries.notes: GH #102. The arrangement lives in an ordinary graph page named by config.edn :tine/favorites-page, because a page is a block tree and therefore merges through the oplog (managed) and Concord (Direct) for free, where a JSON/EDN blob is last-writer-wins - the documented cause of Obsidian's total bookmark loss across Sync. config.edn :favorites stays the flat Logseq-readable membership list, written as a one-way projection in pre-order. Members are [[links]] so renames follow for free (the staleness class GH #79 fixed by hand). DEPTH (Martin, 2026-08-25): the arrangement is ONE node type at any depth - a bullet is a favorite when it is nothing but one [[link]] and a label otherwise, and both nest. There is no group/item split, which is why arbitrary depth costs nothing and why every bullet round-trips verbatim at every depth. The previous one-level model dropped everything below the second level and re-emitted a favorite's own children as unrelated top-level bullets; that is fixed by construction. Drop depth is measured from where the drag STARTED, not the row's left edge, so a plain vertical drag can never nest by accident; depthRange applies the outliner rule and clamps rather than inventing intermediate parents. Labels are plain text, never pages. Deleting a label moves what it held up one level and never unfavorites anything (Capacities' contract; Obsidian's folders lose the reference). Unfavoriting a parent promotes its children rather than taking them with it. The page is created LAZILY - only once a label or a nested row exists - so a user who never nests anything sees no change at all. The rendered arrangement is derived from live membership on every read, so the sidebar cannot show an unfavorited page or miss a favorited one. LIVE: editing the arrangement page (in Tine's editor or outside) now re-reads it and projects membership, so a hand edit is visible immediately - which is also the keyboard route for reordering. Tine's own write is ignored by revision so it is not adopted as an external edit. config.edn is re-read too (see NON-UI CONFIG-LIVE-RELOAD). STILL NOT CLOSED: :favorites is written wholesale from the frontend's list, so a favorite added in Logseq inside the reload window can still be overwritten by the next star toggled in Tine; closing that needs a three-way merge in set_favorites' own atomic_update closure. Keyboard reorder IN THE SIDEBAR (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7) remains the deliberate GH #211 deferral. HARNESS DEBT: scripts/shot-favorites-groups.mjs was written to prove the CSS layout because jsdom applies no layout, but it does not run on this box - every invocation is killed before producing output, with no stray process and no PID pressure. The indent is now asserted in jsdom as an inline padding-left per depth, which is stronger than the previous class-only assertion, but the painted result is still VISUALLY UNVERIFIED.

entries.title: A clean quit is not reported as an unclean close on the next launch
entries.notes: Internal report, 2026-08-28, found by the absence-sweeps E2E journey. mark_clean_shutdown() was placed after tauri's App::run(), which never returns (the event loop exits the process via std::process::exit), so the flight recorder's session-active marker survived every quit and every subsequent launch showed the sticky 'Tine did not close cleanly last time' warning. Present since the flight recorder shipped (GH #343, 271885b2). Fix hooks RunEvent::Exit, the callback tauri delivers before exiting. Wiring is untestable at unit layer (needs the real event loop); the E2E journey's clean-close-honored phase is the observation-boundary proof: unclean toast present on reopen before the fix (diag-1 artifacts), absent after. Retrofitted to GH #426 on 2026-08-31: this internal find and the Linux/Windows half of that public report are the same defect, and the reporter's own diagnostics attachment (v0.6.98, build 94579a0, which predates the fix) confirms it — its previous session records runtime.started and 26 later events but no runtime.clean_shutdown. The mobile half of #426 is a different orderly-end question and is UI-MOBILE-BACKGROUND-FALSE-UNCLEAN-TOAST-426.

entries.title: Switching to a Settings section that loads something does not close and reopen the whole dialog
entries.notes: User outcome: choosing a section inside Settings changes the pane, and the dialog, its section list and the search box stay where they are. Classification: blocking stateful UX. Root cause: Settings is lazy() and mounted under a FALLBACK-LESS <Suspense> in App.tsx, so any panel that starts loading a resource as it mounts suspended the whole dialog and Solid removed it from the document until the load settled — the user saw Settings vanish and come back. The three sections the reporter names are exactly the three whose panels load on mount: Journals (the template list), Backups & recovery (the journal-filename inventory) and Graph (the home-page picker, confirmed by removing HomePageField and watching the Graph case go green). Sections with nothing to load never flickered, which is why the report names only those three. Fix: a <Suspense> inside settings-pane-body, so a section that loads shows a blank pane for that moment instead of taking the dialog with it; the modal has a fixed height, so nothing resizes. Fixed at the boundary rather than at each of the three panels so a fourth loading panel cannot reintroduce it. The regression reproduces the App.tsx wrapper deliberately — rendering Settings bare hides the defect entirely — and asserts synchronously after the click, because the flash is one frame wide and a settled assertion cannot see it.

entries.title: The Settings dialog opens at the size it was last left at
entries.notes: User outcome: someone who maximizes Settings finds it maximized the next time they open it, and after restarting Tine; someone who restores it finds it small. Classification: blocking stateful UX (a preference the user re-enters several times a day). GH #287 shipped the control as deliberately transient and #427 asked for the opposite on the reporter's case: 'I never want the small version — having to press the control on every open is a small tax paid several times a day.' The state moved out of the dialog into src/settingsLayout.ts, because Settings is lazy() and unmounts on close, and is persisted through the same device-local app_bool store the other remembered preferences use. Hydrated at startup rather than at dialog mount, so a remembered wide dialog opens wide instead of opening small and snapping. Default is unchanged (small) for anyone who never presses the control. #287's 'does not persist across modal close/reopen' assertion was the old contract and is replaced, not grandfathered; both directions of the store round trip are asserted, since either half alone would look right while the setting evaporated on restart.

entries.title: A mobile app the OS reaps while backgrounded is not reported as having closed uncleanly
entries.notes: User outcome: backgrounding Tine on a phone or tablet and coming back later does not greet the user with 'Tine did not close cleanly last time'. Classification: blocking stateful UX (a permanent false alarm that trains users to ignore a real crash notice). Root cause: the flight recorder's session-active marker is removed at the one orderly end the app knew about, the desktop event loop's RunEvent::Exit. iOS and Android have no such moment — the OS suspends a backgrounded app and reaps it later without notice — so the marker always survived and EVERY launch warned. The reporter said exactly that: 'It does happen every time in iOS/iPadOS. The OS kills the app when in background so I am having this issue all the time.' Fix: on mobile the recorded session follows webview visibility, ending when the app is hidden and restarting when the user returns, so a crash they witness is still reported and a reap they never see is not. Desktop is deliberately excluded, because a minimised window is still a live session and honouring visibility there would hide exactly the background crashes the recorder exists to catch; that exclusion is asserted on both sides (src/sessionActivity.test.ts 'never ends a desktop session on visibility', and the cfg gate pinned by debug.rs 'visibility_ends_a_session_only_where_the_os_reaps_backgrounded_apps'). Fail-before is causal: making the marker removal a no-op turns debug.rs 'a_session_the_os_reaps_after_backgrounding_is_not_reported_unclean' red while its companion 'a_session_that_dies_after_coming_back_is_still_reported_unclean' stays green. EVIDENCE LIMIT: no iOS or Android runtime was available, so the recorder contract and the platform gating are proven at unit layer on Linux and the on-device toast is not; confidence stays moderate. One further warning is expected on the first launch after upgrading, from the marker the previous build left behind.

entries.title: The sheet Add row control stays put and legible while a wide table scrolls horizontally
entries.notes: User outcome: on a table wider than its container, '+ Add row' is readable before, during and after a horizontal scroll, and dragging the table sideways moves the cells rather than the label. Root cause: the add-row button is a `grid-column: 1 / -1` item of a `width: max-content` grid inside `overflow-x: auto`, and its centred label therefore sat at the midpoint of the whole table. Fail-before measurement at a 420px viewport over a 1325px table: label at +647px unscrolled and -258px fully scrolled, outside the viewport at both extremes; after, +27px at both. The exact offset and the sticky implementation are not user contracts.

entries.title: Long-pressing a page link on a touch platform opens Tine's menu without the OS selection bar over it
entries.notes: User outcome: a long press on a page link or tag shows Tine's context menu alone — no platform Copy/Look Up bar stacked over it and no menu action highlighted as selected text. Classification: blocking stateful UX. Root cause: the hold is simultaneously the OS's text-selection gesture, owned by a native recognizer; preventDefault() on Tine's SYNTHETIC contextmenu cannot cancel it, and iOS fires no contextmenu for touch. Only refusing to be selectable stops it, so .page-ref/.tag are user-select:none on touch platforms and the .ctx-* menu surfaces are unselectable everywhere. Accepted tradeoff: on a phone or tablet a rendered page link can no longer be included in a text selection sweep; desktop selection is unchanged, and that asymmetry is itself asserted. The stale claim in longPress.ts that preventDefault suppressed native selection has been corrected in place.

entries.title: The fold-all guide covers the left edge of the per-block fold arrow, so aiming at the arrow folds the whole subtree
entries.notes: User outcome: aiming at a block's fold arrow folds that one block, never the whole subtree. Classification: blocking stateful UX. Root cause: the children guide (the vertical line that folds EVERY descendant) is position:absolute z-index:1 with left:-9px width:14px, while the child row's 18px fold arrow begins at the children container's left edge — so the guide was painted over the arrow's leftmost 5px and answered clicks there. The reporter, three weeks into daily use, kept hitting it; aim cannot adapt to a control that is invisibly on top of another. Fix: the guide is now 5px wide, centred within 0.5px on the 1px line it draws, and stops exactly at the arrow's edge, so the arrow keeps all 18 of its pixels. OG provenance: og-1.0.0 components/block.css .block-children-left-border is 4px wide at left:-1px, i.e. it hugs its line and overlaps nothing; the reporter's 'hitbox is smaller' is accurate. The reported 'right-skewed' is not literally true — the old box was centred on the line to within 0.5px — but the harm was real and is what the fix targets. Fail-before is quantitative: restoring left:-9px/width:14px makes the guard report the guide covering exactly 5px of the per-block controls at x=29..33. jsdom applies no CSS layout, so a headless-Chromium geometry guard is the only layer that can see this; scripts/check-outline-guide-hitbox.mjs asserts the user-visible contract (covers no pixel of the neighbouring controls, centred on its own line, no larger than the per-block control) rather than the constants.

entries.title: The left sidebar's resize strip is drawn over its scrollbar, so the scrollbar cannot be grabbed
entries.notes: User outcome: the left sidebar's scrollbar can be grabbed and dragged with the mouse. Classification: blocking core operation (the surface is scrollable but its scrollbar is unreachable). Root cause: .sidebar-resizer is position:absolute right:0 width:7px z-index:20 inside .left-sidebar, and .left-sidebar-scroll fills that same box — so on any platform whose scrollbar consumes layout width (Windows/WebView2 is the reported one) the drag strip was painted over the outer 7px of a 10px scrollbar. Resizing worked; scrolling by mouse did not, which is exactly what two Windows reporters described. Fix: .left-sidebar-scroll reserves a transparent right border of --sidebar-resizer-width, the same token the strip's width now uses, so the scrollbar column and the drag column are disjoint and moving a few pixels left off the strip reaches the bar, as the reporter asked. The border is transparent so the sidebar background is unchanged; the mobile drawer, where the strip is hidden, sets the border back to 0 and keeps its full width. Siblings reviewed: .rs-resizer sits at the RIGHT sidebar's LEFT edge while that pane scrolls on its right, and the main pane's scrollbar ends where the right sidebar begins, so neither pair overlaps — the left sidebar was the only conflicting pair. The frameless-window .grip-e strip does overlay the rightmost 4px of whatever pane touches the window edge, but that is the ordinary window-edge resize zone every frameless app has, not this defect. Fail-before is quantitative: removing the gutter makes the guard report the strip covering 7.0px of the 10px scrollbar. EVIDENCE LIMIT: no Windows runtime was available. jsdom applies no CSS layout and this headless Chromium always draws overlay scrollbars, so scripts/check-sidebar-resizer-scrollbar.mjs reproduces the Windows condition with scrollbar-gutter:stable in the fixture; the column geometry is proven, the WebView2 bar itself is not, so confidence stays moderate.

entries.title: Clicking past the last glyph of a block that ends in hidden markup puts the caret before the closing delimiter
entries.notes: User outcome: clicking in the empty space to the right of a block's last line puts the caret at the end of what the editor will show, so Enter starts the next block instead of splitting the construct. Classification: blocking stateful UX (the caret is one byte short, inside markup the reader cannot see). Root cause: the click was answered by the span map, which for a trailing construct like *italics* legitimately maps the end of the visible text to the source byte BEFORE the invisible closing delimiter — a valid interior offset, so the existing 'mapping failed' fallback never ran. Proven at the mapping layer: for `*some text in italics.*` the end of the rendered text maps to 22, one short of the 23-character source. Fix: recognise the click by WHERE it landed, not what it landed on — beyondFinalGlyph() in src/render/spans.ts asks whether the point lies past the rightmost glyph of the bottom-most line band, and Block.tsx consults it before the span map, returning the end of the editor's VISIBLE value (not raw.length, which counts hidden property lines). Deliberately geometric rather than per-syntax: a rule keyed on emphasis would have to be repeated for bold, inline code, strikethrough and the Org forms, and a rule that snapped any span-end to the construct end would break precise clicks inside formatted text. Siblings preserved: a precise interior click still maps exactly (asserted for the italic body), a click past an EARLIER wrapped line still lands at that line's end rather than the block's, and the trailing-link behaviour of GH #34 is unchanged because there the editable end and the span end coincide. Real-app proof drives WebKitGTK pointer clicks at computed run-out coordinates for three trailing constructs (emphasis, strong, inline code); fail-before was reproduced by running the same extended journey against the pre-fix release binary. The geometric probe declines where the environment has no layout engine: jsdom does not implement Range.getClientRects, and calling it there threw out of the click handler and disabled the whole rendered-block edit gesture until guarded (pinned in src/render/clickSpans.test.tsx). It also measures only the IN-FLOW content: a float is drawn hard against the block's right edge, and one TALLER than the line it rides owns the bottom band, so a single range over the whole block answered "where does the text end?" with the full content width and the past-the-end caret was dead in that block. The live case is `{{img … right}}` — measured in the running app at wrapper right 1080 / bottom 545.2 against text right 665.5 / bottom 542.2, fail-before caret 85 of 86 and pass-after 86, asserted by scripts/e2e-clickcaret-repro.mjs block 11. Out-of-flow children are skipped recursively because that wrapper sits inside the inline tree. The reference-count badge floats too but is shorter than the line and never defined the bottom band: it is the control in the same scenario (block 9), after a synthetic fixture wrongly indicated otherwise.

entries.title: Ctrl/Cmd+click and Alt+click on a block bullet zoom in place instead of opening a new tab or the other pane
entries.notes: User outcome: a modifier held over a bullet sends the block where the same modifier sends a [[page ref]] — Ctrl/Cmd or middle-click to a background tab, Alt to the other pane, Shift to the right sidebar — instead of silently zooming in place. Classification: blocking stateful UX (the gesture is learned from links and the app answered it differently in one place). Root cause: the bullet's own handler tested `e.shiftKey` alone rather than the shared decision in src/linkGesture.ts, so every other modifier fell through to the plain zoom. Sibling swept in the same change: the read-only reference bullet in RefBlocks.tsx (linked references, query results, embeds) had the identical Shift-only handler. Both bullets also ran their own onMouseDown and skipped GH #207's other half, so shift-range text selection and middle-button autoscroll / PRIMARY-paste were never suppressed there; they now go through internalLinkMouseDown, asserted in both files. Not covered here: the ref-count badge and the query workspace's result rows, which are separate surfaces that ignore all modifiers today — recorded as follow-ups, not part of this row. Fail-before: with the handlers reverted, the Ctrl and Alt assertions fail in both files while the Shift and plain-click controls pass.

entries.title: A global shortcut whose only modifier is Alt does not fire while the caret is in a block
entries.notes: User outcome: a shortcut the user bound to a bare Alt chord (the reporter's Alt+S for the next tab) fires with the caret in a block, the same as it does everywhere else in the app. Classification: blocking core operation (the binding is configured and simply does not run in the place the user spends most of their time). Root cause: the global dispatcher's while-typing guard admitted only `mod`/`ctrl` chords, so Ctrl+Alt+S worked and Alt+S did not. Alt now counts as a modifier there. Only `scope: "global"` commands with a `run` are matched by that dispatcher, so the block editor's own bare-Alt bindings (alt+f/alt+b/alt+w/alt+d/alt+u/alt+k/alt+l) are untouched, and an Alt chord nothing is bound to still reaches the textarea unprevented — asserted directly, because on macOS that event is an Option-composed character. Fail-before: with the guard reverted the Alt+S assertion fails while both control assertions pass.

entries.title: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter on the highlighted search result navigates in place instead of opening a background tab
entries.notes: User outcome: driving search from the keyboard reaches the same destinations as the mouse — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter fans the highlighted result into a background tab and leaves the switcher open, so several results can be opened without searching again. Classification: blocking stateful UX (the modifier is already learned from the click established by GH #288 and did nothing on the keyboard). Root cause: the Enter handler implemented Shift and Alt but had no Ctrl/Cmd rung, so the chord fell through to plain navigation. Page and block rows only, matching the click; create and command rows keep their existing single action. Fail-before: with the new branch removed the switcher closes and no tab is added.

entries.title: A block's bullet sits on the vertical centre of that block's first line of text, at every heading level and under every typography theme
entries.notes: User outcome: the bullet reads as belonging to its line, and a column of bullets lines up with the column of text. Classification: flexible presentation, accepted as a defect because a user reported it on daily use. Root cause: .block-controls carried a literal height:26px chosen to match .block-content's line-height, but .block-content also has padding:2px 0, so centring inside the shorter column put every bullet in the graph exactly 2.00px above the middle of its own first line - and 4.00px above it under the editorial-serif typography preset, which raises the line box to 30px but could not move a literal. Fix: two tokens (--ls-block-line-height, --ls-block-content-pad-y) own the first line in one place; .block-content, .block-editor and the bullet column all derive from them, and the typography preset retunes the token instead of the content rule. Fail-before is quantitative: the guard reported 71 misplaced bullets, -2.00px on every measurable journal block and -4.00px under editorial-serif; after the fix every plain block is within 0.5px. Headings keep their own taller bullet column (.bullet-h1/h2/h3, ~1.2x the heading line box) and are deliberately unchanged - h1 still sits ~2px off its line centre; the guard holds them within 3px so a change to the ordinary column cannot silently drag them. jsdom applies no CSS layout, so headless-Chromium geometry is the only layer that can observe this; the oracle is derived from each element's own computed padding-top and line-height, never from a pixel constant, so a fix that cancelled one error with one constant would fail under the serif preset.

entries.title: The reference-count badge sits on the block's first line, not on its last, when the block wraps
entries.notes: User outcome: the count badge stays where the reader expects it - level with the top of the block, matching what a one-line block already looks like - instead of dropping to the bottom-right corner of a long block. Classification: flexible presentation, accepted because a user reported it. Root cause: .block-refs-count is float:right and was emitted as the LAST child of .block-content, so the float attached to the line box that was current when the browser reached it, i.e. the final line. Measured before the fix on the kitchen-sink referenced block: badge top = content top + 2px on one line (right), +28px once the column was narrowed enough to wrap (one full 26px line too low). Fix: the badge is emitted FIRST inside .block-content, so its float attaches to the first line box and the text flows around it; a right float does not disturb the block's own box, so nothing reflows vertically. Checked in a browser that a leading block-level child (code fence, table, blockquote) is not overlapped either - each shrinks or clears beside the float. The badge keeps its behaviour (plain click opens the referrers panel, shift-click opens the block in the right sidebar). Two layers: the browser guard measures the wrapped case that only CSS layout can show, and a render test pins the DOM order the float placement depends on, since jsdom can see the order but not the geometry.

entries.title: In a RIGHT-sidebar item, only the page title is the link; the blank space beside it belongs to the reorder drag
entries.notes: User outcome: dragging a right-sidebar item to reorder it does not open the page instead, and the hand cursor does not follow the pointer out over empty space. Classification: blocking stateful UX - the reporter lost his place while reordering, on Windows 10. SURFACE CORRECTION: the reporter meant the RIGHT sidebar; the v0.6.981 fix changed the LEFT sidebar, which both missed this issue and caused the regression reported as GH #468. Root cause: the markup already made only the anchor a link - navigation lives on <a class=rs-item-title> in RightSidebar.tsx, not on the row - but .rs-item-title carried flex:1 1 auto, so the ANCHOR ELEMENT stretched across the rest of .rs-item-head. Every pixel right of a short title was still the <a>, painting cursor:pointer over the head's own cursor:grab and racing the reorder drag. Fix: flex:0 1 auto so the anchor is sized to its own text (min-width:0 keeps it the element that ellipsises), plus margin-left:auto on .rs-close, which had been relying on the stretched title to push it to the right edge. Evidence at the browser layer because which element sits under a given pixel is CSS layout, which jsdom does not apply; necessity gate: the harness reports a 221px overhang against pre-fix CSS. OG provenance: Logseq makes only the text clickable, and Tine agrees here - the pane where Tine deliberately diverges is the left sidebar, see UI-SIDEBAR-LEFT-ROW-FULL-CLICK-468.

entries.title: The whole left-sidebar row opens its page, including the blank space beside a short name
entries.notes: User outcome: clicking anywhere in a left-sidebar row - favourites, Recent or All pages - opens that page, so a page named 'test' is not a target a few characters wide. Classification: blocking stateful UX; the row-shaped hover highlight promises a row-shaped target, and the reporter hit the gap in normal navigation. Root cause: v0.6.981 gated click and auxclick on a .nav-page-label wrapper (the onLabel helper) for GH #464, and moved cursor:pointer onto that label, so the rest of the row became inert. Fix: the gate is removed in all three lists and cursor:pointer is back on .nav-page; the .nav-page-label span stays, because it is what ellipsises a long name in an overflow:hidden row. Favourites also lose the cursor:grab they carried since GH #211: a row that opens a page on click has to say pointer, and grab said the opposite. INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE FROM OG (Martin, GH #468 thread): Logseq makes only the text clickable; Tine makes the whole left row clickable because the larger target is worth more than the parity here. It costs the reorder nothing, and that is the load-bearing part: rowReorder's 4px threshold and post-drag click suppression are what separate a reorder from a click, not an un-clickable region, so the same file asserts that a drag grabbed by the blank space reorders WITHOUT navigating. The context menu still takes the whole row. Necessity gate: 4 of the 6 render assertions fail against pre-fix Sidebar.tsx, and the two that pass are exactly the invariants the change had to preserve. The browser harness adds the affordance the render layer cannot see - the row's cursor and that nothing else owns the row's spare pixels.

entries.notes: The pre-fix highlighted background began in the bullet control track, crowding ordinary dots and numbered ordinals. entries.title: Dollar-delimited LaTeX renders as math when it is directly inside ordinary Markdown emphasis
entries.notes: User outcome: inline and displayed dollar math remains typeset when a whole agent response or another Markdown span is italic, bold, struck, or highlighted. Classification: blocking core operation because the same valid math already renders outside emphasis and formatting surrounding prose must not erase its semantics. Fail-before on exact Tine base d427c43b with the vendored lsdoc v0.5.6 WASM: the focused render test found zero .math descendants and left both delimiters as literal text inside <em>. The parser fix is deliberately lsdoc-only: v0.5.7 recognizes top-level-valid dollar fragments through a root-owned linear index at grammar-bounded nested emphasis sites, while Tine's existing recursive renderer and MathView consume the resulting Latex child unchanged. Org, invalid dollar shapes, code spans, synthetic triple emphasis, and non-emphasis link labels remain unchanged. Anonymized-graph acceptance covered all 1,045 files with freshly rebuilt v0.5.6 and v0.5.7 release parsers: the baseline had zero differences; v0.5.7 produced exactly three, and the fail-closed classifier proved all three as md-nested-dollar-latex with 1, 2, and 3 accepted candidates respectively, leaving zero unclassified corpus changes.

Root cause is one shared invariant, not this one surface: `existing_page_names` answers over page names UNION alias names, so an alias edit changes the answer while creating and deleting no file -- and the batched exists-cache was keyed only on (graphEpoch, pageInventoryRev), neither of which moves for a property-only save. Root cause is ownership, not the clause menu: `the user pressed outside` had no producer, so each popover answered it or did not. Twelve popovers across the app had hand-rolled a capture listener (drifting between mousedown/pointerdown and document/window) and four had not: QueryBuilder's clause menu and add-filter picker, and the two PdfViewer popups were correct only by accident of where the user clicked. The popover trigger counts as inside, so its own click still toggles. Also corrected in the same file: `+ sort` re-opened rather than toggled when its trigger was clicked while open, the only one of the four that did not toggle. Two existing tests asserted states that only jsdom could reach (two clause menus open at once; a modal header press leaving a child menu open) and were rewritten to the real-browser outcome. The reporter's own conditional is the proof of the root cause: adding text to the page FIRST made the sidebar editable, because the main pane had run the re-seed on their behalf. Both halves of `always somewhere to type` -- the phantom empty bullet for an empty body and the trailing `+ Add block` -- lived inside PageSection, so every other page surface silently lacked them. Fixed by extracting them into one exported producer, PageTypingTarget in src/components/Page.tsx, used by both PageSection and the sidebar's PageItem; `ensureEmptyBlock` stays the single emptiness authority, so a properties-only page counts as empty on both surfaces without a second predicate. entries.notes: User harm: the copy button floated in the middle of the Linked References row while the Unlinked one sat at the right edge, so two near-identical sections read as different controls. Root cause is a flexbox rule, not a value to tune: `.reference-export-toggle` and `.reference-filter-toggle` each claimed `margin-left: auto`, and two auto margins SPLIT the free space between them rather than one absorbing it. Unlinked References has no filter button, so its copy button kept the whole gap and landed at the edge. Fixed by giving the header one owner of that push -- the first trailing button takes the free space, the rest sit on the row gap -- and by rendering copy last in Linked References so it lands on the same edge as the section that has copy alone. Measured in a real engine (headless Chromium over the built app), not modelled: before, the two right edges were 766px and 1030px in a 1100px viewport; after, both are 1030px. jsdom applies no layout, so the render test pins only the DOM order that the CSS rule depends on.

entries.notes: User harm: pressing Tab on a bullet inside a block embed indented the bullet correctly but threw the caret out of the embed onto the source copy of the same block elsewhere on the page, so the next keystrokes landed somewhere the user was not looking. Root cause is a shared invariant, not the Tab key: a store operation that reopens the editor must name the surface the caret belongs to, and `indentBlock`/`outdentBlock` did not take one. With no surface named, `editing()` in Block.tsx deliberately prefers the non-`ref:`/`embed:` rendering (the agenda-copy rule), so the editor remounted on the source. `splitBlock`, `mergeWithPrev` and `mergeWithNext` had already been given the parameter; indent, outdent and the Alt+Shift+Up/Down move had been missed. Fixed by giving all three the same `editingSurface` parameter that the split/merge family takes and passing `structuralSurface()` from the command table, and the class is now held at zero by a source scan over src/store.ts (proven to fire by reverting one call). Deliberately NOT changed in this packet: the paste and template-insert sites in Block.tsx also drop the surface, but they focus a NEWLY CREATED sibling, which may legitimately fall outside the embed's subtree -- pinning those to the embed surface could mount no editor at all. That is a separate question about which surface renders a new block, recorded rather than guessed. Evidence layer: jsdom render, driving the literal keydown path over a host page that renders the target block twice (once in the embed, once as an ordinary root) -- with a single rendering there is no wrong surface to land on and the bug is invisible. Not re-run natively; the surfaces here are DOM structure, not WebKitGTK layout.

The backend is not wrong: the host block's own text really does contain the search term. The missing rule is at the presentation boundary, which is the only layer that knows which block hosts the query. OG parity provenance: logseq/og at 6e7afa8e, frontend/components/query/result.cljs get-query-result computes `remove-blocks (if current-block-uuid [current-block-uuid] nil)` with the comment 'exclude the current one, otherwise it'll loop forever', and frontend/db/query_react.cljs custom-query-result-transform removes exactly those uuids -- the host block only, NOT its children, which remain ordinary results. Tine now does the same in one place per membership decision: `withoutHostBlock` over the RefGroups (all three fetch paths funnel through it) and the equivalent filter over `execution.hits`, because the Search presentation renders those hits directly rather than the groups. Diagnostics and the query explanation keep the unfiltered execution: the hit was really found, it is simply not shown to itself. Breadth: every query-execution call site was inventoried -- the tag-page query (Page.tsx), the virtual query workspace and the quick switcher have no host block at all, so QueryMacro is the whole class. Evidence layer: jsdom render over the real Block/QueryMacro path with the backend mocked to answer honestly; the fail-before run reproduces the recursion literally (the list rendered 'query' nine times).
